project.goal: Discover AI trends, synthesize source-grounded knowledge, and maintain a reusable library for all agents.
acceptance: Scout can maintain the knowledge library through project events, not only heartbeat.
The library index remains useful for agents looking for reusable knowledge.
Maintenance favors consolidation, source grounding, and downstream reuse over creating shallow new files.

context.migration_note: 2026-06-12: moved Scout knowledge library from /app/agents/scout/knowledge to /app/projects/scout-knowledge-lib/knowledge with a compatibility symlink at the old path.
context.migration_first_principle: First preserve and index existing knowledge. Consolidation happens only after source-aware review.

ongoing-research.goal: Continuously discover AI trends from multiple sources and synthesize findings into the knowledge library.

context.note: This is a perpetual process — there is always new knowledge to explore. Each child represents an ongoing source channel.

library-maintenance.goal: Periodic library health: consolidate new duplicates, update INDEX.md, archive stale findings, improve synthesis quality.

context.note: Triggered by knowledge-planner workflow when project.owner.requested events arrive. Reacts to library drift by creating or updating concrete child work for current health signals.
context.seed_note: Runtime health details belong in .state/tasks/tree.json and library-health packets, not in the boot seed.

existing-knowledge-migration.goal: Move existing Scout knowledge into the project-owned domain workspace without losing provenance.
acceptance: Existing knowledge files are preserved under the project workspace.
The old agent-local knowledge path remains available as a compatibility symlink.
Historical second-brain outputs are copied as migration evidence rather than merged blindly into durable notes.

library-inventory-and-index.goal: Review knowledge/INDEX.md and library navigation so agents can find existing notes before creating duplicates.
acceptance: Index covers the current markdown notes in the library.
Index links validate against existing files.
Known duplicate clusters are recorded for task-tracked consolidation.

dedupe-and-quality.goal: Find duplicate, stale, or low-context knowledge notes and consolidate them without losing source-grounded findings.
acceptance: At least one concrete duplicate/stale cluster is improved or an exact no-op reason is recorded.
No shallow bulk rewrites are made just to satisfy a metric.

triage-inbox-imports.goal: Triage the 89 research drafts in knowledge/inbox/ (imported 2026-06-13 from root cleanup). Decide per-file: merge unique findings into canonical notes, archive as provenance, or delete as noise.
acceptance: Each inbox batch has a triage decision: merge, archive-as-provenance, or delete.
Unique findings from inbox files are merged into existing canonical notes rather than creating new top-level notes.
Inbox file count drops substantially after triage.
INDEX.md inbox section is updated to reflect triage progress.

context.approach: Process by source (XHS, HN, arXiv) not by import batch. Most are daily snapshots — extract net-new findings into canonical notes, archive the rest as dated provenance.

source-grounded-synthesis.goal: Fill library gaps identified during inbox triage — add named patterns and protocol coverage to canonical notes where existing notes are thin or silent.
acceptance: New or updated synthesis cites source context and links related notes.
Existing notes are updated before creating a new one.
Each gap identified in triage reports is addressed or explicitly deferred.

context.gaps_from_triage: arXiv: agent security/governance. GitHub: agent harness pattern, skills/plugins, MCP ecosystem, agent testing tooling. See reports/triage/inbox-triage-arxiv-batch.md and reports/triage/inbox-triage-github-batch.md.
context.remaining_gap: Known source-grounding gaps should be reassessed from current library health packets and INDEX state after boot.

adoption-and-reuse-feedback.goal: Review whether Scout and other agents are reusing the library, then feed findings into library structure and task priorities.
acceptance: Reuse/adoption evidence changes the next maintenance priority or records why no action is needed.

context.note: Review current reuse/adoption evidence from live metrics and reports after boot. Do not carry old metric-breach history in the seed.

fill-gap-agent-security.goal: Add a canonical note on agent security and governance patterns. Identified as the #1 cross-cutting theme in the arXiv inbox triage (238 papers) with no existing canonical note.
acceptance: A canonical note covers agent security concerns: prompt injection, tool-use sandboxing, permission models, governance frameworks.
Content is source-grounded from arXiv provenance files, not generated from thin air.
Existing notes (architectures, protocols) are cross-linked where they touch security.

context.origin: Identified as a source-grounded synthesis gap during library migration; reassess from current source reports after boot.

fill-gap-agent-testing-tooling.goal: Decide whether agent testing tooling warrants a canonical note or a section in agent-evaluation.md. Identified as a gap in GitHub inbox triage — testing frameworks, simulation harnesses, and CI patterns for agents.
acceptance: Decision recorded: standalone note vs section in agent-evaluation.md.
If written, content cites specific tools/repos from GitHub provenance.
INDEX.md updated to reflect the new coverage.

context.origin: Identified as a source-grounded synthesis gap during library migration; reassess from current source reports after boot.
